body: I managed to fix the warning on nested CSGCombiner3D nodes by implementing a system that keeps track of what broke. the method `csg_push_warning` is called with the specific problem or `NO_WARNINGS` if everything is OK. - `NO_WARNINGS`: Everything is OK. This is set at the end of `_build_brush` of every CSG node and would reset the warnings. - `NON_MANIFOLD`: Returns the same message as it does in the current version of Godot. Will appear on the root shape if a non-manifold brush was combined with the root shape. - `CSG_SET_NON_MANIFOLD`: `set_csg_brush` now checks with the manifold library if the brush is **manifold**, if this fails it sets it to `nullptr` and throws a warning. - `CSG_MESH_NOT_ASSIGNED`: When a CSGMesh3D is added to the scene it tends to not have a mesh assigned. This warning will be raised at that point. - - `CSG_MESH_NON_MANIFOLD`: Should appear if the `CSGMesh3D` has a non-manifold shape assigned. ~For now, `CSGMesh3D` does not test the meshes to see if they are manifold, so for now this warning only appears if the shape is empty. A non-manifold shape actually causes the root to fail and throw the warning.~ Fixed. `_create_brush_from_arrays` now checks the mesh with the manifold library to see if it's manifold and throws a specific warning. The brush can then fail and not break the CSG tree. - The advantages of this system come from the way CSG brushes are now combined, since they are all treated as siblings, when a shape fails, it just throws a warning, disappears, and the rest of the CSG nodes continue to work normally. ### Nested CSGCombiner3D CSGCombiner3D nodes can be nested and will not throw a warning. And since they don't store a combined CSGBrush anymore, they use less memory and could be used more freely. ### Bugs ~I was unable to make cylinder uvs fully work. The uvs are completely seamless, but the last face of the cylinder will get stretched. I still think it's good enough and that face can be hidden, but I'm open to removing the cylinder uv button until the bug gets fixed by someone else.~ Fixed.
~I was looking at CSG issues, and this PR also closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/111911~ 4.6: This PR: This is another side effect of all CSGs being treated as siblings.

#### Calculate UVs in global space Watching the highlights of 4.7, I realized that boxes are simple, but things like `CSGPolygon3D`s are used for stairs and ramps, and using local coordinates for that could be limiting. So I added a new parameter to `calculate_cube_uv` and `calculate_cylinder_uv` to calculate UVs in **global space** instead of **local space**. A button was added to the bar that toggles this behavior, when enabled, pressing the **Make cube UV** or **Make Cylinder UV** buttons will calculate UVs in global space. There were problems with cylinder UV in global space because the UVs are generated around a center, so I made it so that only rotation and scale are taken into account. The button is in need of a **new icon**, It's using a temporary one. global UV coordinates can be used with rotated or more complex shapes and is specially useful with CSGPolygon3D.
#### Fixes I also managed to fix the cylinder UV problem. One of the calculations was resulting in `-0.0`, which was then converted to `-PI` and causing the bug. A `max` call was added to fix this and the UVs are correctly calculated now:

Note that this PR breaks compatibility in its current state. Example with this scene tree, with `CSGCylinder3D2` being subtractive: Before | After -|- | Overall, I like the improvements from this PR, but we need to make sure existing CSG builds aren't affected by this change. **Testing project:** [csg.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27226599/csg.zip)

It appears to be working, I would still like someone to check the code to make sure I didn't miss something and cause a memory leak. And I would like to hear any advice on how to improve the code. ----- Added the `combine_csg_children` property to `CSGShape3D`. Enabling it combines the children of the CSG node before performing boolean operations, but it has to be enabled on every children with children to perfectly replicate the old behavior. It essentially turns the node into a sort of "sub-root" that acts exactly the same as the root, the children are treated as siblings unless they have `combine_csg_children` enabled. This gives more control over how the CSG works and allows creating more complex "prefabs". Here are two shapes used for testing, the one on the left has the property enabled, the one on the right has it disabled: And here I did a triple-nesting, with a Box that has a cylinder subtracting, and the cylinder has another cylinder subtracting: This needs to rebuild the entire tree every time there's a change because the combined CSG is not saved. For most cases (CSGs with addition) this is not needed, it is most useful when fixing these compatibility issues and achieving different results, so I would recommend trying to do it only when needed. I don't know how to deal with enabling this on old projects but keeping it disabled on new nodes, is there a built-in way of doing this?

Some updates now that I have some free time: I have been using this PR to test its capabilities as a level editor, and I admit, I was wrong with some of my assumptions. Creating this building with hundreds of nested brushes made into prefabs, performance with this PR (during editing) starts to decrease, but is much better when opening the same scene in 4.6. performance goes back up after editing is done, and editing a parallel CSG tree has a normal (higher) performance when there are few brushes, and decreases as more brushes are added. To clarify, this is purely CPU related, and is most likely because the way it is in 4.6, nested brushes get combined and kept in memory, so there are fewer operations happening, while on this PR all brushes have to be combined every time. #### Solutions The solution I can think of is to keep the combined brush in memory like it was done before. Add another pointer to `CSGBrush`, and check it whenever needed to perform operations from the parent, while keeping the `brush` pointer to store altered UVs, Vertices, Materials, etc. Basically, keep a `CSGBrush` to store modified UVs, and a `CSGBrush` with the combined brushes. This second pointer will be `null` when the node doesn't have children, and will not be exposed to gdscript. Then make the `combine_csg_children` property always enabled by default, replicating the old behavior. ----- There's also https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/14839 which asks for a CSGGroup, so maybe I could rename `combine_csg_children` to something like `csg_group`, and when enabled threat all children as siblings instead of combining them. This PR will also no longer close issue 111911, that seems to be a problem related to nested brushes being combined multiple times. There's also the recent fix to performance with autosmooth https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/119543, this PR was working on the previous code and I'm not sure what to do about it now that it's been merged. I'm still busy, but as soon as I have time I will start working on this again.

## Updates I have been making some changes to the code based on the last post. ### Smoothing groups removed After the changes to that part of the code (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/119543), there was a conflict, and the code this was working on is no longer valid due to performance issues. For that reason, I went back on **smoothing groups**, they are boolean again, but left the methods for modifying smoothing groups using integer. **Smoothing groups** could be added in the future using a more performant algorithm. ### Changes to `_get_brush` `_get_brush` was changed first to threat all children as siblings. This turned out to not be very performant, so I went with the alternative of creating a second `CSGBrush` pointer to store the combined brush. This led to the introduction of the `combined_brush` variable. The old code was simplified, and it should behave like in older versions, but nodes can no longer be made into "groups". I kept the old code so this could be implemented in a separate PR in the future (https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/14839). There are now 2 methods for retrieving brushes: - `_get_brush()`: This returns the individual brush of the node. This can be **painted** like before, and due to the changes, making a child node dirty doesn't require rebuilding the un-painted parent brushes. - `_get_combined_brush()`: This returns the combined brush. When calling `_make_painted()`, the node and its parents are set to `children_modified = true`, forcing the combined brushes to be rebuilt. The new system brings mostly advantages. #### Advantages - Root shapes can now be painted! And this includes individual CSG nodes: - - Following this, `make cube uv` and other buttons should now be visible on all CSG nodes. - There is no longer a compatibility breakage with older projects, the behavior is back to the way it was in previous versions. This has also solved the performance issues. - making a node dirty no longer needs to rebuild every parent brush before combining, potentially increasing performance. #### Disadvantages - two CSGBrushes are kept in memory, increasing memory usage. However, data is in the kilobytes, although it could increase with higher poly brushes like CSGMesh. - There are some issues with individual non CSGShape3D children of nodes, such as using a Path3D. The problems seem to have been solved, but more testing is needed to make sure there are no bugs with aabb and brush generation. ### AABB calculation There was a lot of duplicated code so AABB calculation was moved to the `_expand_aabb()` method. ----- More testing is needed, but everything seems to be working now.

### CSGBrush per face AABB removed Related https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/105619 This seems to have been left from before the manifold library was added. The `private` member `brush` (and now `combined_brush`) of type `CSGBrush` stores a `Vector` of `Face`. Each `Face` has things like vertices, uvs, smooth data, And an `AABB`. There was also a `_regen_face_aabb` method that populated these faces with aabbs, which required calling `expand_to`, which does a bunch of checks and some math. This was called in `_unpack_manifold` every time a combined `manifold` `mesh` was converted to `CSGBrush`. It was also called in `build_from_faces`, and in `copy_from`, this last one was also called every time a CSGBrush was prepared to be combined with others. The only CSGBrush in godot is the one in `CSGShape3D` and is private, and the node does nothing with the per face aabb data. Aabbs for the **node** are handled through different means, like `node_aabb`. So both the `_regen_faces_aabb` and the `aabb` in `Face` have been removed. #### Wouldn't this be useful for a face editor? Yes, but no. As part of this PR, ngons were implemented, and methods to obtain the meshes for ngons. These meshes are made out of multiple triangles, and if aabbs were to be needed, it would make more sense to calculate them at that point and not every frame that the brush is being edited like it was until now, or to do it in a different way. ### Improvements to Calculate Cylinder UV Cylinder UV calculation now takes distance into account to better adapt to more varied shapes. The result is seamless along the sides, and can fill some perpendicular faces. It fails only when the face is aligned along X, which is unfortunately where Polygon3D always starts, but this can be solved thanks to global space: CSGTorus on the other hand just refuses to work, but Cube UV gives pretty good results instead. ### Known Issues * ~Just found a bug, when adding a CSG node, it appears empty. The Rebuild button needs to be pressed to make it work. I need to investigate this later.~ Fixed.

### Cleaup Some unused code from this PR was removed. * Originally I had the idea to invert the order of vertices to make the triangles backface, because a face editor needs them. But **backfaces** are not implemented in gizmo collisions, all faces are treated as double sided when using `p_gizmo->add_collision_triangles()` . So the code was removed entirely, this is a problem that needs it's own proposal and changes to core. * The code for displaying lines was skipping the root shape because of how it was working when this PR started, so this was simplified. Code for removing duplicated lines was also removed, as it's not worth the code complexity and possible performance issues. Shapes are being displayed with ngons again: * * * Added tooltips to the buttons to explain what they do: *

### New testing script The previous test script was rushed and only meant to make sure everything was working, the version I posted here was also outdated compared to the one I was using. I made a new test script that works by selecting a brush and then selecting a face or vertex to make changes. It has better named functions and buttons, works per ngon, and is updated: [face_editor.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28903427/face_editor.zip) While working in this script I also made some corrections to the code in the documentation. ### Scaling UV artifacts Using this new script I discovered some artifacts that happen after scaling on brushes with Cube UV mapping. My best guess is these are from floating point errors as the scaled UV gets divided. To clarify, these are because of the UVs stored in CSGBrush, they get saved and loaded and can be replicated easily by scaling by 0.5 a couple times, then by 2.0 on a CSGBox with Cube UV mapping applied: #### Solutions For UV calculation there is already a parameter for setting scale, it's just missing a triple-spinbox control for setting it, and could be implemented per face, so that should help those trying to do simple scaling of UVs. However, I have added the idea of a **UV editor window** to the proposal, to allow manually fixing any artifacts and for more advanced UV editing. ### Preparations for a UV editor This is nothing big, just the methods `get_brush_uvs` and `set_brush_uvs`, these can be used to create a UV editor like there is in trenchbroom and unreal in the future. All they do is return all the UVs and set all the UVs of the CSGBrush respectively.
